comp_0.description:
What it does The decision rule for the Parallel Executor: it decides when the group is finished and what to do about failures.

How it works Watches the slots as they complete, applies the configured failure strategy to any that errored or timed out, and reports when the group is done. It makes no calls of its own and holds no configuration.

Configure Nothing. Set the timeout and failure strategy on the FSM instead.

In and out In: the state of the running slots. Out: the decision to finish, and the joined results.

Use it when It comes with the Parallel Executor template. You do not add or configure it separately.
comp_0.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: policy
name: Parallel Executor Policy
description: >
  Internal control policy for the Parallel Executor. Merges every branch's
  response into one payload and stamps it with fan-out metadata.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none
    response_data_contract: dynamic
    response_data_contract_reason: >-
      One key per branch label from the executor's `states` configuration, plus
      `_parallel_metadata`; the branch set is configuration-determined.
    request_data:
      results: object (optional) - Branch label to response_data mapping.
      errors: object (optional) - Branch label to error text mapping.
      failure_strategy: string (optional) - How branch failures were treated.

policy_states:
  - state_1
  - state_2
comp_0.name: PARALLEL EXECUTOR - POLICY (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
comp_0.short_description: The decision rule for the Parallel Executor: it decides when the group is finished and what

comp_1.description:
What it does The entry point of the Parallel Executor template. It accepts the input that every parallel slot will receive.

How it works Passes the incoming data and any accompanying file straight through to the executor, which hands the same input to each slot.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the caller's request. Out: the same, unchanged, into the executor.

Use it when It comes with the Parallel Executor template. You do not add it separately.

comp_2.description:
What it does The engine of the Parallel Executor template. It starts every slot together and joins the results.

How it works Dispatches all configured slots concurrently, waits for them within the timeout, and collects what came back. Its policy decides how to treat a slot that failed or timed out, according to the failure strategy you chose.

Configure
- States - the slots to run concurrently and their components.
- Timeout seconds - the ceiling on how long to wait for stragglers.
- Failure strategy - fail the whole step on any error, or continue with the successful
results.

In and out In: the data handed to every slot. Out: the collected results.

Use it when It comes with the Parallel Executor template - configure it there rather than adding it on its own.
comp_2.manifest_yaml:
extension_type: fsm
name: Parallel Executor
description: >
  FSM layer that fans out to its wired state slots concurrently as separate Ray
  tasks, waits for every result, then merges them through the paired policy.

input_ports:
  - port_name: input
    port_type: in
    artifact_type_input: optional(json)
    artifact_type_output: json
    response_data_contract: dynamic
    response_data_contract_reason: >-
      The merged payload is whatever the paired policy returns from merging the
      branches named by the `states` input parameter, so the key set is
      configuration-determined.

state_ports:
  - port_name: state_1
    artifact_type_input: json
    artifact_type_output: json
  - port_name: state_2
    artifact_type_input: json
    artifact_type_output: json

policy_ports:
  - port_name: policy
    artifact_type_input: none
    artifact_type_output: none

input_parameters:
  - name: timeout_seconds
    type: number
    label: Timeout (seconds)
    default: 300
    description: Hard limit on how long the fan-out may take.
  - name: failure_strategy
    type: select
    label: Failure Strategy
    options: [wait_all, fail_fast, ignore_failures]
    default: wait_all
    description: How to treat a branch that raises.
  - name: states
    type: text_long
    label: States Configuration
    default: "[]"
    description: JSON array of port_name/label pairs naming the slots to fan out to.

comp_3.description:
What it does The exit of the Parallel Executor template. It returns the joined results of all the slots.

How it works Takes the collected results and returns them as the result of the nested run, so the parent flow can carry on. It adds nothing of its own.

Configure Nothing.

In and out In: the joined results of the parallel slots. Out: the same data, as the template's result.

Use it when It comes with the Parallel Executor template. You do not add it separately.

orchestration.description:
What it does Runs several steps at the same time and waits for them all, instead of one after another. Use it when the steps do not depend on each other.

How it works Wire a component into each slot; every slot starts together and the template waits for them to finish before continuing. Total time is roughly the slowest step rather than the sum of all of them. A timeout bounds the wait, and you choose what should happen if one of them fails: stop the whole thing, or carry on with the results you did get.

Configure (on the FSM component inside)
- States - the slots to run concurrently, and what runs in each.
- Timeout seconds - how long to wait before giving up on stragglers.
- Failure strategy - whether one failure fails the whole step, or the run continues with
whatever succeeded.

In and out In: the data given to every slot. Out: the results of all slots, collected together.

Use it when
- Several independent lookups or model calls can happen at once.
- You are fanning the same question out to multiple models or sources to compare.
- A slow set of steps has no ordering requirement and latency matters.
orchestration.name: PARALLEL EXECUTOR (SYSTEM, READ-ONLY)
